body.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\), the nested-split conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), and
\[
 \sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1).
\]
Then, pointwise under \(P\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)
 \ \Rightarrow\ N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},
\]
\(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and
\[
 P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
For a locally uniform regularity extension, fix \(T<\infty\) and a class \(\mathcal S\) of bounded DQM path scores, and write \(P_{n,t,s}=P_{t/\sqrt n,s}\).  Suppose uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\): the construction-sample bridge and multiplier bounds defining \(d_{c,n}\) and \(d_{0,n}\), the sieve approximation \(\alpha_{J_n}\), the calibration exponential-moment and concentration bounds \(\eta_{G,n},\eta_{c,n}\), the positive-eigenvalue gap, cutoff stability, coefficient and weight envelopes, and \(\Gamma_n=o_p(1)\) all hold under \(P_{n,t,s}\); the root-\(n\) mixed-bias gauge is \(o_p(1)\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\to\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) in \(L^2\) and its squared family is uniformly integrable; and
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\sqrt n\{\theta(P_{n,t,s})-\theta(P)\}-tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\right|\to0,
\]
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\log\frac{dP_{n,t,s}^n}{dP^n}
 -\frac{t}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^ns(O_i)+\frac{t^2}{2}E_P[s^2]\right|=o_P(1),
\]
with a uniform Lindeberg condition for \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\), and suppose the arrays \(P_{n,t,s}^n\) and \(P^n\) are mutually contiguous uniformly on the declared class.  Then the preceding asymptotic linear expansion, variance consistency, and centered Gaussian limit hold uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\).  In particular, the estimator is regular and locally efficient on every such uniformly controlled contiguous path class.
body.justification: The mixed-bias and conditional cross-fit calculations give pointwise asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, and Wald coverage once learned efficient-signal convergence is supplied.
body.gap: That convergence is unresolved, and pointwise rates do not yield the locally uniform contiguous-path expansion needed for regular efficiency.
body.consumer: Wald reporting from the general learned affine ensemble remains conditional rather than certified under the current primitive assumptions.
body.proof_tex:
For \(i\in\mathcal I_k\), put
\[
 f_k=\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), \(\max_k\|f_k\|_2=o_p(1)\).  Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\), the function \(f_k\) is fixed and the observations in \(\mathcal I_k\) are independent of it.  Therefore
\[
 E\!\left[\left.\left\{\sqrt n(P_{n,k}-P)f_k\right\}^2\right|\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\right]
 \le C\|f_k\|_2^2=o_p(1),
\]
where fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) makes the fold-size factor bounded.  Conditional Chebyshev followed by a finite union bound gives
\[
 \sum_k\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}(P_{n,k}-P)f_k=o_p(1).
\]

For a learned cell, the two exact bridge identities at the base law give
\[
 P\{S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)\}
 =-E[I_a(\widehat q-q^0)(\widehat h-h^0)].
\]
Conditioning on \((A,Z,X)\) and on \((W,X)\), respectively, bounds its absolute value both by
\[
 \|T_a(\widehat h-h^0)\|_2\|\widehat q-q^0\|_2
 \quad\text{and by}\quad
 \|\widehat h-h^0\|_2\|T_a^*(\widehat q-q^0)\|_2.
\]
Summing over cells and using the total-variation envelope gives
\[
 \max_k|P\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)|
 \le CL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}
 =o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Combining the conditional empirical term and this drift proves
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).
\]
The summands on the right are i.i.d., mean zero, square-integrable, and have variance \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).  They satisfy the Lindeberg condition because, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 E\!\left[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf 1\{|\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}|>\epsilon\sqrt n\}\right]\to0.
\]
The cited \(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\) therefore gives the asserted Gaussian limit.

For variance estimation, write \(\widehat\psi_i-\theta(P)=\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+f_{k(i)}(O_i)\).  Conditional Markov inequality gives
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_i f_{k(i)}(O_i)^2=o_p(1),
\]
because its conditional expectation is bounded by \(\max_k\|f_k\|_2^2=o_p(1)\).  Cauchy--Schwarz makes the empirical cross term with \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) negligible.  To verify the remaining law of large numbers using only \(E\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2<\infty\), truncate \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\) at level \(M\).  Chebyshev's inequality handles the bounded truncated variables, while Markov's inequality bounds the empirical and population tails by \(E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf 1\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2>M\}]\), which tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Hence \(n^{-1}\sum_i\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)^2\to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).  Since \(\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)=O_p(n^{-1/2})\), centering by \(\widehat\theta_n\) does not alter the limit.  Thus \(\widehat V_n\to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\), and positivity gives ratio consistency.  The product of the standardized numerator and \(\{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)/\widehat V_n\}^{1/2}\) consequently has the standard normal limit by the continuous-mapping argument; continuity of the normal distribution at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) proves pointwise Wald coverage.

Now impose the displayed locally uniform conditions.  Every preceding bound depends on the law only through \(\Gamma_n\), the mixed-bias gauge, the fold-size constant, and the stated moment envelopes.  Taking the supremum over \((s,t)\) in each conditional Markov or Chebyshev bound therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{s\in\mathcal S,|t|\le T}
 \left|\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P_{n,t,s})\}
 -n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})(O_i)\right|
 =o_{P_{n,t,s}}(1).
\]
The uniform \(L^2\) continuity and uniform integrability imply convergence of the corresponding variances, while the stated uniform Lindeberg condition and \(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\) yield the centered triangular-array Gaussian limit.  The assumed contiguity makes the base-law and local-law negligible remainders compatible, and the linear LAN term together with the displayed target expansion shows that centering at \(\theta(P_{n,t,s})\) removes exactly the local mean shift \(tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\).  Consequently the centered limit is \(N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}\), uniformly on the declared class.  The same uniform second-moment argument proves variance consistency.  This is precisely regularity on those contiguous path classes; because \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is the canonical gradient under \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), the limiting variance is the local efficiency bound.
